corrected_value.authors: Illingworth, S., & Bishop, D. V. M.
corrected_value.title: Atypical cerebral lateralisation in adults with compensated developmental dyslexia demonstrated using functional transcranial Doppler ultrasound

decisions.location: Conclusions, lines 2385-2395 (see also Methods lines 1281-1295; Discussion lines 2183-2189; References lines 2869-2875)
decisions.quote:
In a large sample of twins oversampled for language problems, the present study failed to 

find evidence for atypical laterality, either in terms of handedness or cerebral lateralisation for 

language, in those with DLD. Theories have proposed that disruption to the typical left 

hemisphere dominance for language may be a neurobiological correlate of language problems 

(e.g. Annett, 2002; Bishop, 2013; T. J. Crow et al., 1998), and empirical studies of very small 

samples have supported that view (Illingworth & Bishop, 2009; Whitehouse & Bishop, 2008).
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this work. In Methods (lines 1281-1295), the authors explicitly include children impaired on literacy measures in the DLD group on the basis of Illingworth & Bishop's (2009) fTCD finding of reduced left-hemisphere language lateralisation in dyslexia, and in both the Discussion (lines 2183-2189) and Conclusions (lines 2385-2415) they explicitly state that their fTCD comparison failed to replicate the reduced left-hemisphere language dominance reported by Illingworth & Bishop (2009) (doi:10.1016/j.bandl.2009.05.002) and Whitehouse & Bishop (2008). Because shipped row 2411 captures only Whitehouse & Bishop (2008) (blind target 3), Illingworth & Bishop (2009) is a genuinely distinct missing replication target.
